reference_title: GSA Alternate Path Analysis and Design Guidelines for Progressive Collapse Resistance (October 24, 2013, Revision 1, January 28, 2016)
scope_note: 35 figures cataloged: Chapter 2's applicability flow chart (Figure 2.1), all 15 SURVIVING numbered figures in Chapter 3 (Figures 3.7-3.21 -- Figures 3.1 through 3.6 are listed in the front-matter List of Figures with blank captions and a page reference of 7, but the body text states 'This UFC section is removed in its entirety, including the following figures: Figure 3.1. ... Figure 3.6.' (Section 3.1, Tie Forces) -- there is no image to catalog for these six numbers, and they are deliberately OMITTED here), all 8 figures in Appendix B (structural-analysis definition diagrams: joint/connection rotation, yield/plastic rotation, panel zone, story drift -- content identical in kind to UFC 4-023-03 Appendix B), all 6 figures in Appendix C (steel connection-type illustrations supporting Table C1.1), and the 5 building-geometry figures from Appendix D (Figures D2.1-D2.5, the reinforced-concrete worked example this package validates against in reinforced_concrete.py/redundancy.py -- Figure D3.1 and all Figure D4.x/D5.x SAP2000-screenshot/analysis-result figures are deliberately OMITTED as narrow, software-workflow-specific content, mirroring ufc_collapse's own Appendix D figure-catalog scope). All 35 pages were located directly during full-document text extraction (each figure's own page marker was read alongside its caption) and independently cross-checked against this document's own front-matter List of Figures (printed pp. vii-x) -- both sources agree at every entry; page_estimated=false throughout. Appendix E (the parallel structural-steel worked example: building plans, SAP2000 screenshots, load-pattern and DCR-result figures) is NOT cataloged at all -- narrow, software-workflow-specific content for one example building, not general design figures of the kind this package catalogs elsewhere (mirrors ufc_collapse's decision to skip its own analogous Appendices E/F/G in their entirety; see the package __init__.py docstring scope note).

figures.caption: Applicability Flow Chart
figures.description: Flow chart implementing Section 2.3's Facility Security Level (FSL) applicability logic: FSL I/II never require these Guidelines; FSL III/IV require them at 4+ stories (Alternate Path AND Redundancy); FSL V requires them at any story count (Alternate Path only). See applicability.fsl_applicability().

figures.caption: Definition of Force-Controlled and Deformation-Controlled Actions, from ASCE 41 [10]
figures.description: The generalized component force-versus-deformation curve (Types 1, 2, 3) and the e/g ratio definitions underlying Section 3.2.5's classification rule; identical in content to UFC 4-023-03 Figure 3-7. See alternate_path.classify_action().

figures.caption: Removal of Column from Alternate Path Model
figures.description: Illustrates Section 3.2.9.1's beam-to-beam continuity assumption across a removed column, and the full-clear-height removal extent between lateral restraints.

figures.caption: Location of External Column Removal
figures.description: Plan diagram of the Section 3.2.9.2.2 FSL III/IV exterior column removal locations: middle of the short side, middle of the long side, corner, and penultimate (adjacent-to-corner).

figures.caption: Location of Internal Column Removal
figures.description: Plan diagram of the Section 3.2.9.2.3 internal column removal locations within underground parking or uncontrolled-public-access areas: middle of the short side, middle of the long side, and corner of the uncontrolled space.

figures.caption: Location of External Load-Bearing Wall Removal
figures.description: Plan diagram of the Section 3.2.9.2.4 exterior load-bearing-wall removal locations, including the 2H-in-each-direction corner removal extent.

figures.caption: Location of Internal Load-Bearing Wall Removal
figures.description: Plan diagram of the Section 3.2.9.2.5 internal load-bearing-wall removal locations within underground parking or uncontrolled-public-access areas.

figures.caption: Allowable Extents of Collapse for Interior and Exterior Column Removal in Plan
figures.description: Plan-view illustration of Section 3.2.10.2's existing-building disproportionate-collapse allowance (15% exterior / 30% interior of the floor area directly above the removed element). See alternate_path.disproportionate_collapse_allowance().

figures.caption: Allowable Extents of Collapse for Interior and Exterior Column Removal in Elevation
figures.description: Elevation-view companion to Figure 3.13, showing the allowance is limited to the single floor level directly above the removed element.

figures.caption: Loads and Load Locations for External and Internal Column Removal for Linear and Nonlinear Static Models (Left Side Demonstrates External Column Removal; Right Side Shows Internal Column Removal)
figures.description: Defines the perimeter A-B-C-D within which the increased gravity load (GLD/GLF/GN) is applied for a column removal, per Equations 3.3, 3.5, and 3.8, and the region searched for the governing mLIF/rotation ratio.

figures.caption: Loads and Load Locations for External and Internal Wall Removal for Linear and Nonlinear Static Models (Left Side Demonstrates External Wall Removal; Right Side Shows Internal Wall Removal)
figures.description: Wall-removal companion to Figure 3.15, for load-bearing-wall structures.

figures.caption: Plan View of Strength Definitions for Load Redistributing Systems
figures.description: Plan diagram defining the single-structural-bay extent of horizontal members contributing to a load redistribution system's design strength QR (Equation 3.15, Section 3.4.2.2). See redundancy.load_redistribution_system_strength().

figures.caption: Elevation View of Strength Definitions for Load Redistributing Systems
figures.description: Elevation diagram showing multiple load redistribution systems up the height of the building, whose average strength QR_bar is computed by Equation 3.16.

figures.caption: Plan View of Stiffness Definitions for Load Redistributing Systems
figures.description: Plan diagram, analogous to Figure 3.17, for the flexural stiffness KR of a load redistribution system (Equation 3.18, Section 3.4.2.3). See redundancy.load_redistribution_system_stiffness().

figures.caption: Definition of Stiffness based on Various Support Conditions
figures.description: Support-condition-dependent flexural-stiffness formulas for a uniformly loaded beam (fixed-fixed, fixed-pinned, etc.); the Appendix D worked example uses the fixed-fixed case, KC=384*Ec*Icr/L^3 (see redundancy.fixed_fixed_flexural_stiffness()).

figures.caption: Elevation View of Stiffness Definitions for Load Redistributing Systems
figures.description: Elevation diagram showing multiple load redistribution systems up the height of the building, whose average stiffness KR_bar is computed by Equation 3.19.

figures.caption: Joint and Connection Definition
figures.description: Illustrates the joint (central region where members attach) versus the connection (the link transmitting moment/shear/axial actions), for steel moment and reinforced concrete framing. Identical in content to UFC 4-023-03 Figure B-1.

figures.caption: Joint and Connection Rotations
figures.description: Sketches distinguishing rigid-body joint rotation (Gamma) from connection rotation (theta), measured relative to the joint.

figures.caption: Definition of Chord Rotation (from ASCE 41 [10])
figures.description: Shows how, in a frame, the chord rotation equals the connection rotation theta when joint rotation is separately accounted for.

figures.caption: Definition of Yield Rotation, Plastic Rotation, and Total Rotation
figures.description: Moment-versus-rotation curve defining the yield rotation theta_y (elastic limit), plastic rotation theta_p (post-yield, non-recoverable), and their sum, the total rotation theta.

figures.caption: Plastic Hinge and Rotation
figures.description: Shows a discrete plastic-hinge model inserted into a numerical frame model, measuring both elastic and plastic rotation (the elastic portion often ignored due to its small size).

figures.caption: Panel Zone
figures.description: Illustrates the steel-frame column-web panel zone (region of high shear stress within the joint boundaries of a fully restrained connection), whose deformation measure is the plastic angular shear rotation.

figures.caption: Story Drift
figures.description: Defines story drift (ratio of lateral deflection at the top of a wall segment to its overall height) as ASCE 41's nonlinear deformation measure for load-bearing wall structures.

figures.caption: Vertical Wall Deflection (Drift)
figures.description: Adapts the story-drift deformation measure (Figure B1.7) from horizontal seismic drift to VERTICAL deflection due to a removed wall section, for progressive-collapse analysis of load-bearing wall structures.

figures.caption: Fully Restrained Moment Connections or Shear Connections
figures.description: Illustrates the Fully Restrained (FR) steel connection types of Table C1.1: WUF, Welded Flange Plates, Welded Cover-Plated Flanges, Bolted Flange Plates, Free Flange, Welded Top/Bottom Haunches, and Reduced Beam Section.

figures.caption: Partially Restrained Moment Connections or Shear Connections
figures.description: Illustrates the Partially Restrained (PR) steel connection types of Table C1.1: Top and Bottom Clip Angles, Bolted Double Split Tee, and Bolted End Plate.

figures.caption: Weak Axis Moment Connection or Shear Connection
figures.description: Illustrates the Shear Tab Connection (with or without composite floor deck) of Table C1.1.

figures.caption: Kaiser Bolted Bracket® Fully Restrained Connection
figures.description: Schematic of the proprietary Kaiser Bolted Bracket SMF moment connection (cast-steel haunch brackets bolted to the column flange).

figures.caption: SidePlate® Fully Restrained Connection
figures.description: Schematic of the proprietary SidePlate SMF moment connection (full-depth side plates with fillet welds), whose m-factors and modeling parameters are digitized in structural_steel.py (Tables 10-11).

figures.caption: SlottedWeb™ Fully Restrained Connection
figures.description: Schematic of the proprietary SlottedWeb SMF moment connection (WUF-like, with extended web slots at the weld access holes).

figures.caption: Building Floor Plan (Levels 2-6)
figures.description: Floor plan of the Appendix D 8-story reinforced-concrete example building (FSL IV, controlled lobby, no below-grade parking) -- perimeter moment frames, pan-joist/slab floor system. See reinforced_concrete.py and redundancy.py validation anchors.

figures.caption: Building Roof Plan
figures.description: Roof plan of the Appendix D example building, showing reduced roof-beam reinforcement relative to the typical floor level.

figures.caption: Building Elevation along GL A
figures.description: Exterior elevation of the Appendix D example building along gridline A (a perimeter moment-frame gridline).

figures.caption: Building Elevation along B-F (Interior)
figures.description: Interior elevation of the Appendix D example building spanning gridlines B through F.

figures.caption: Building Elevation along Gridline 1 and 4
figures.description: Exterior elevations of the Appendix D example building along the short-side gridlines 1 and 4.
